I believe that there are at least two different and distinct levels of "dangerous precedents."

The first is "dangerous precedents" set by an individual sub, within its individual sub.

The second is "dangerous precedents" set by the entire site, within the context of the entire site.

For reasons that I would hope to be obvious, I consider the second to be MUCH more of a threat than the former, since the latter threaten the entire site, while the former only threatens individual subs.

I consider the actions of ProtectVoat generally, and kevdude specifically, to be establishing a dangerous precedent site-wide - the precedent that a single group of users should be seen to possess sufficient authority to decree what other subs and other mods may, may not, must or must not do. Therefore I oppose their actions - not because I reject their principles, but because I do not believe that the authority they presume to rightly possess should exist AT ALL. It's not that I don't want them decreeing what other mods on other subs may, may not, must or must not do, but because I don't want ANYONE to do that. I want the power to determine what is done on a particular sub to remain within that particular sub and not be seen to be something that can and should be applied by third parties.

Authority misused within an individual sub can indeed destroy that sub. But that damage is contained in that sub, and Voat provides a built-in way to avoid that damage - I can simply go to a different sub.

Authority misused site-wide can do more than destroy individual subs - it can destroy the entire site. That is, in fact, exactly what destroyed Reddit. I don't want to see that happen here, therefore I will stand against those who seek authority site-wide, and yes - even though that means that individual subs can and will institute destructive rules. That's a shame, but it's better than the alternative. Much better a sub destroyed than the entire site.
